pairs.question: Qualis est ista puella, quam tecum duxisti?
pairs.answer: Filia regis est, quam in uxorem habeo.
pairs.derivation: Father questions son on his return. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Sed dic mihi,' before the interrogative and the tag 'Ait ille:' before the answer. Question is the father's interrogative clause; answer is the son's full reply sentence. Normalized capitalization and the terminal '!' to '?'.

pairs.locus: Gesta Romanorum 53 (De perfectione vitae / Focus faber)
pairs.question: Quare legem editam violas?
pairs.answer: Legem illam servare non possum, quia omni die octo denarios oportet me habere, et illos sine labore non potero acquirere.
pairs.derivation: Emperor interrogates the smith. Dropped the framing 'Ait imperator:' and the preceding rhetorical 'Carissime, quid est, quod audio de te?' to keep the operative interrogative; dropped the tag 'Ait ille: "Domine,' from the reply. Answer ends at the first full stop. Normalized capitalization.

pairs.locus: Gesta Romanorum 53 (De perfectione vitae / Focus faber)
pairs.question: Et quare octo denarios?
pairs.answer: Omni die per annum duos denarios teneor dare, quos mutuavi in iuventute, duos accomodo, duos perdo, duos expendo.
pairs.derivation: Emperor follows up; the smith itemizes his eight pence. Dropped speech tags 'Ait imperator:' and 'Qui ait:'. Answer ends at the first full stop, before 'Ait imperator: "De istis manifestius..."'.

pairs.locus: Gesta Romanorum 61 (De praemeditatione / Socrates and Alexander)
pairs.question: Carissime, quis est dominus tuus, de quo talia dicis, quod servus eius est dominus meus?
pairs.answer: Dominus meus est ratio, servus eius voluntas, sic est ergo, quod tu per voluntatem tuam regnum tuum et non per rationem huc usque gubernasti.
pairs.derivation: Alexander asks Socrates to name his master. Dropped framing 'ait ei rex:' and 'Ait ille:'. Question carries its own referent for 'talia'. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the elaborating 'Ideo servus domini mei, hoc est voluntas, est dominus tuus.'

pairs.question: O bone magister, ob quam rem affligitur anima tua?
pairs.answer: Filiam regis sub tali condicione desponsavi, quod, quocumque tempore ipsa in societate mea moriatur, ego vitam meam amittam, et iam ad mortem infirmatur, et haec est causa doloris mei.
pairs.derivation: An old man asks why Socrates grieves. Dropped framing 'ait:' and 'Et ille:'. Answer is the full reply (one sentence ending in 'haec est causa doloris mei').

pairs.question: Domine mi reverende, qualis domina ista est?
pairs.answer: Domina nostra soror regis est.
pairs.derivation: The knight's wife asks who the lady is; he answers. Dropped framing 'ait:' and 'Qui ait:'. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the elaborating 'Iura mihi per deum...'.

pairs.question: Carissime, unde venis?
pairs.answer: De terra sancta venio.
pairs.derivation: The returning knight is asked by the king's messenger where he comes from. Dropped framing 'ait ei:' and 'Qui ait:'. Self-contained short exchange.

pairs.question: Et quales rumores habetis?
pairs.answer: Dominus meus rex mortuus est et corpus suum ad unum de castris suis est ductum.
pairs.derivation: Follow-up to the previous exchange; the messenger reports the news. Dropped framing 'Et ille:'. Answer is the full reply sentence.

pairs.question: Quomodo est de domino meo?
pairs.answer: Dominus vester mortuus est et eius corpus de terra sancta translatum est ad castrum suum, et cum patre vestro sepelietur.
pairs.derivation: The lady asks the messenger about her brother (the king). Dropped framing 'ait ei domina:' and 'Qui respondit:'. Answer is the full reply sentence.

pairs.question: Domine, quo tenditis?
pairs.answer: Hospitium quaero.
pairs.derivation: A citizen asks Gregorius where he is heading. Dropped framing 'ait ei:' and 'Et ille:'. Self-contained short exchange.

pairs.question: Domine, qualis est civitas illa et quis dominus istius terrae?
pairs.answer: Carissime, unum virum valentem imperatorem habuimus, qui mortuus est in terra sancta, qui nullum heredem praeter suam sororem post se reliquit.
pairs.derivation: Gregorius asks his host about the city and its lord. Dropped framing 'dominus Gregorius hospiti dixit:' and 'At ille:'. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the elaborating 'quidam dux eam in uxorem petiit...'.

pairs.question: De qua progenie es tu, dicite mihi?
pairs.answer: Scias sine dubio, quod de longinqua terra sum ego.
pairs.derivation: The lady asks Gregorius his lineage. Dropped framing 'ait:' and 'Qui ait:'. Skipped the non-answering preamble 'Ista est mirabilis quaestio;' and advanced the answer start to the operative clause.

pairs.question: O carissime, dic mihi causam, quare adivicem estis tam fideles?
pairs.answer: Domine, a pueritia quilibet alteri fidem dedit, ut in omnibus fideles essemus.
pairs.derivation: The judge asks the two thieves why they are so faithful to each other. Dropped framing 'Iudex respexit eum et ait:' and 'Et ille:'. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the elaborating 'Et haec est causa...'.

pairs.question: Quare sic mecum agis? Indica mihi! Rogo te.
pairs.answer: Nolo, et haec est causa: Si veritatem tibi dixissem, unum scilicet filium tuum velles eum diligere et alterum odio habere, et ideo volo, quod ambos aequaliter diligas et nutrias.
pairs.derivation: The queen presses the king for the truth. Dropped framing 'At illa:' and 'Et ille:'. Kept the contiguous utterance (interrogative plus plea). Answer ends at the natural stop before 'et cum ad aetatem legitimam veniunt, tunc tibi veritatem pandam...'.

pairs.locus: Gesta Romanorum 121 (De gloria mundi et luxuria)
pairs.question: Carissima, qua de causa de lecto singulis noctibus surgis?
pairs.answer: Super arborem fici omni nocte residet philomena, quae tam dulciter cantat, quod oportet me surgere et eam audire.
pairs.derivation: The husband asks his wife why she rises every night. Dropped framing 'ait ei:' and 'Quae respondit:'. Answer is the full reply sentence.

pairs.locus: Gesta Romanorum 195 (cf. The Merchant of Venice)
pairs.question: Quid tibi dabo, quod possum una nocte tecum dormire?
pairs.answer: Mille marcas florenas.
pairs.derivation: The knight asks the emperor's daughter her price. Dropped framing 'ait ei:' and 'Quae ait:'. Self-contained exchange.

pairs.locus: Gesta Romanorum 195 (cf. The Merchant of Venice)
pairs.question: Quam securitatem mihi praestabis?
pairs.answer: Quidquid vis.
pairs.derivation: The merchant asks the knight what security he will give. Dropped framing 'Qui ait:' and 'Et ille:'. Self-contained exchange.

pairs.question: Quantum diligis me?
pairs.answer: Certe plus quam me ipsam.
pairs.derivation: Theodosius asks his eldest daughter how much she loves him. Dropped framing 'dixitque filiae seniori:' and 'At illa:'. Self-contained exchange.

pairs.question: Quantum diligis me?
pairs.answer: Tantum sicut me ipsam.
pairs.derivation: Theodosius asks his second daughter the same question. Dropped framing 'ait ei:' and 'At illa:'. Self-contained exchange.

pairs.question: Quantum me diligis?
pairs.answer: Tantum sicut vales et non plus neque minus.
pairs.derivation: Theodosius asks his youngest daughter how much she loves him. Dropped framing 'ait ei:' and 'At illa:'. Self-contained exchange.
